summary: Radar for 2026-10-17, GLP-1 focus only. The strongest new lead is regulatory and fits the gray-market "what's confirmed" format that has worked for us. On Oct 14, the UK's medicines regulator (MHRA) and West Midlands Police seized more than 12,000 fake retatrutide and tirzepatide pens (about £2M) in Birmingham. Two more items arrived the same week: Futurism and the Atlanta Journal-Constitution (AJC) are covering the black market, and a Penn medRxiv preprint (not yet peer-reviewed) found Reddit users of unapproved retatrutide most often reported increased appetite, fatigue and insomnia, not the stomach side effects seen in the trials. Second: an exploratory SURPASS-CVOT analysis (AJMC, Oct 15) reports tirzepatide vs dulaglutide in type 2 diabetes with heart disease and a history of heart failure: 18.2% vs 21.5% had death or a heart-failure event over about 4 years. That fits our named-drug head-to-head format. Third: the orforglipron CHMP recommendation (Oct 16) is the best dated-status question for Instagram. Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 is the best next-gen decoder for long-form, but it was tested against placebo, so the title must not suggest it beat tirzepatide. Evergreen follow-ups still worth making: SURMOUNT-5 stomach side effects, why some people lose 20% and others much less (refreshed by Yahoo, Oct 15), regain after stopping (WKRN, Oct 17) and protein with strength training. Held back or caution: cancer-risk associations, cocaine-craving animal data, eye scare stories, the schizophrenia cohort (poor audience fit), and anything about switching or compounded products. 'Switching from compounded semaglutide to tirzepatide' and anorexia or telehealth loopholes stay rejected.

candidates.topic: Fake retatrutide and tirzepatide pens: UK's MHRA seized 12,000+ counterfeit pens (~£2M) in a Birmingham raid on Oct 14, 2026, as US reports of black-market 'retatrutide' harms grow
candidates.angle: Calm 'what's confirmed vs not (Oct 2026)': retatrutide is investigational and not approved anywhere (it isn't authorised in the UK; FDA hasn't approved it); MHRA says seized products had no checks on safety, quality or what's inside. Pay-off: the only legitimate tirzepatide comes through a prescriber and a registered pharmacy. Never name sellers or say how to buy.
